title: Bless'd Be the Everlasting God
description: Bless'd Be the Everlasting God in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 26, headed “Hope of heaven by the resurrection of Christ, 1 Peter 1. 3-5”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bless'd be the ev-er-last-ing God, The Fa-ther of our Lord, Be his a-bound-ing mer-cy prais'd, His maj-es-ty a-dor'd.

lines: When from the dead he rais'd his Son,
And call'd him to the sky,
He gave our souls a lively hope
What tho' our inbred sins require
Our flesh to see the dust!
Yet as the Lord our Saviour rose,
Saints by the power of God are kept
We walk by faith as strangers here
Till Christ shall call us home.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
